messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Re: NA/NaN warning
messages.body_plain:
Thought I would comment on this for future users, if you want to find the combination of parameters that cause a NA/NaN during an optimization I have I used the following code.

options(warn = 2); # any warning gets upgraded to an error and so will kick out of optim() or nlminb() if encountered.
obj = MakeADFun(...)
opt = nlminb(obj$par, obj$fn, obj$gr)
# Error in nlminb(mod_2$par, mod_2$fn, mod_2$gr ...)
#(converted from warning) NA/NaN function evaluation
obj$env$last.par

> function is not well defined. This is not a problem if convergence in the end is OK. I guess
> tracepar = TRUE can help you find out for which parameter value this happened, and hence
> teach you something about the structure of your model.

messages.subject: Does glmmTMB provide dispersion for bbmle AIC?
messages.subject_clean: Does glmmTMB provide dispersion for bbmle AIC?
messages.body_plain:
Hi!

I am currently running models with glmmTMB that are overdispersed. To compare the models with bbmle, I can use either AICtab or ICtab. I know that I need to use a qAIC to compare these models. As I understand the bbmle functions, AICtab will automatically use a dispersion attributes within objects put into it. ICtab requires a supplied dispersion value to run its qAIC.

I have tried both on my models and they provide completely different delta AIC values. Does anyone know if glmmTMB provides objects with dispersion values already? (The line is in the summary, but not sure if it is usable by other packages). This is the only way I can determine which AIC output is accurate.

Much thanks,
Abby Walter

messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Does glmmTMB provide dispersion for bbmle AIC?
messages.subject_clean: [TMB users] Does glmmTMB provide dispersion for bbmle AIC?
messages.body_plain:
This question (and other questions about glmmTMB) is probably more
appropriate for r-sig-mix...@r-project.org ...

  You do *not* need to use quasi-AIC to compare models that use
parametric distributions to handle overdispersion; quasi-AIC is only
needed when you use *quasi-likelihood*, i.e. you fit the model as though
it wasn't overdispersed (Poisson, binomial, etc.) and then do a post-hoc
correction for estimated overdispersion.

  cheers
   Ben Bolker

messages.subject: TMB and the sandwich formula
messages.body_plain:
For conditional/quasi likelihood it can be usefull to use the sandwich-formula for approximating the covariance matrix of the parameter estimates.

The formula is simple enough (see e.g. http://www.stat.umn.edu/geyer/5601/notes/sand.pdf) and for untransformed parameters you only need the gradient and the hessian of the objective function. So in that aspect TMB is great.  However, If you want to use the deltamethod fon quantities that are transformations of the parameters I still need the derivative of transformation , that is, the "phi'" in the documentation of sdreport(). Usually this is Automatic by just using adrep() on transformed quantities, but the calculation seems to be hidden. So, my question is:

- Is it possible to retrieve the derivative of the transformation "phi" somehow?
- If not, can you work your way back using the gradient, hessian and the estimated covariance Matrix? (I Guess you can at least find the value of phi^1 %*% (phi^T)^(-1)

argument sandwich = TRUE in the  sdreport() is on my (sand-) wish list.

Cheers,

Geir

messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Posterior samples for ADREPORTed variables for tmbstan fit
messages.subject_clean: [TMB users] Posterior samples for ADREPORTed variables for tmbstan fit
messages.body_plain:
Can you get all these values by iterating over the posterior samples that is output from tmbstan into the obj$report(). I have attached some pseudo code to hopefully help, probably not the must efficient but I think it should work.

obj = MakeADFun(...)
tmb_stan_par_post = tmbstan(obj = obj, chains = 1,...); # one chain for simplicity, you will have to append multiple chains
## assuming we satisfy Bayesian checks convergence to an equilibrium posterior
for (i in 1:nrow(tmb_stan_par_post)) {
   rep_values = obj$report(tmb_stan_par_post[i]) ## might not be exactly right syntactically, but hopefully you get the gist
   # save values that you want, rbind or other ways to store specific values of the list object rep_values
}

On Tue, Feb 26, 2019 at 3:55 PM Steven Delean <jsde...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi all,
>
> I would like to obtain posterior samples from ADREPORTed variables from a tmbstan fit.
>
> As a reproducible example, I have edited the linreg.cpp from the TMB examples. I am interested in the variable "xint" as follows:
>
> // Simple linear regression.
> #include <TMB.hpp>
> template<class Type>
> Type objective_function<Type>::operator() ()
> {
>   DATA_VECTOR(Y);
>   DATA_VECTOR(x);
>   PARAMETER(a);
>   PARAMETER(b);
>   PARAMETER(logSigma);
>   ADREPORT(exp(2*logSigma));
>   Type nll = -sum(dnorm(Y, a+b*x, exp(logSigma), true));
>   Type xint = -a/b;
>   ADREPORT(xint);
>   return nll;
> }
>
> I use the following R code (again edited from the examples):
>
> library(TMB)
> compile("linreg.cpp")
> dyn.load(dynlib("linreg"))
> set.seed(123)
> data <- list(Y = rnorm(10) + 1:10, x=1:10)
> parameters <- list(a=0, b=0, logSigma=0)
> obj <- MakeADFun(data, parameters, DLL="linreg")
> obj$hessian <- TRUE
> opt <- do.call("optim", obj)
> opt
> opt$hessian ## <-- FD hessian from optim
> obj$he()    ## <-- Analytical hessian
> rep <- sdreport(obj)
> summary(rep)
>
> So I can obtain a summary of the ADREPORTed variable as above from the TMB analysis.
>
> My question: Using tmbstan, how can I sample this variable, or access the posterior samples if they are already accessible please?
>
> library(tmbstan)
> init.fn <- function() list(a=0, b=0, logSigma=0)
> fit <- tmbstan(obj = obj, chains = 1, init = init.fn)
> fit
> head(post <- as.data.frame(fit))
>
> I followed the recent post "Getting REPORTed variables from a tmbstan fit" but as the xint variable is not a 'parameter' in the model, I could not see how that solution could work.
>
> Thanks for your time,
> Steve
>

In your simple example if it's a straight function of parameters you can just apply that function to the posterior samples and get a posterior for that function.
